new_statements.quote: Il n'y a pas à proprement parler d'accent tonique, il existe seulement une manière d'intonation que seul l'usage permet d'acquérir.
new_statements.translation: There is, properly speaking, no tonic (word) accent; there is only a kind of intonation that can be acquired only through usage.
new_statements.citation: Monteil, Charles. 1915. Les Khassonké: monographie d'une peuplade du Soudan français. Paris: Ernest Leroux.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (archive.org leskhassonkmon00montuoft, 562 pp., text present) and its. At PDF page 436 = printed p. 408 (running head 'MONOGRAPHIE DES KHASSONKÉ', Livre III 'Langue', Préliminaires 'Sons élémentaires'), immediately after the two numbered pronunciation conventions and before the 'Voyelles.' heading, the text reads exactly: 'Il n'y a pas à proprement parler d'accent tonique, il existe seulement une manière d'intonation que seul l'usage permet d'acquérir.' — verbatim as quoted (extracted text and line 17743-45 both confirm). Context read: pp. 406-409 are Monteil's transcription key for 'le dialecte des gens du Khasso' ('un dialecte malinké, corrompu par des Peul et influencé par…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Monteil denies a word accent in Khassonké and attributes the audible prominence pattern to 'intonation' learned by ear, i.e. (in modern terms) lexical/grammatical tone; no syllable position is singled out. This matches the modern family picture (Vydrin 2017: stress absent in most Mande languages; West Mande languages have two level tones) and Koité-Herschel's tone-marked Xasonga data, but the dedicated modern phonology (Koité-Herschel 1981, 1982) could not be opened.
new_statements.exceptions: none; vowel length is treated separately (marked with a circumflex). Note the contemporaneous pan-Manding claim of Delafosse 1929 §441 (weak pitch-based accent on the word-final syllable), which is not Khassonké-specific and predates tonal analysis.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level remark in a pronunciation guide to the author's transcription; pre-phonological (1915) colonial description of the Khasso (Kayes/Médine) variety.
new_statements.identity_note: Monteil 1915 describes the Khassonké of the Khasso (Kayes/Médine area, Mali) = xaas1235 proper. Vydrin 2017 treats '(Western) Maninka-Xasonka' as a single language with Khassonké as a barely distinct normed variety; Glottolog keeps Western Maninkakan (west2500, mlq) separate under the Xasonka node (xaso1239). Delafosse 1929's 'MN = malinké du nord ou khassonké' statements are pan-Manding, not variety-specific.

sources.citation: Delafosse, Maurice. 1929. La langue mandingue et ses dialectes (Malinké, Bambara, Dioula), vol. I: Introduction, grammaire, lexique français-mandingue. Paris: Geuthner.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: pp. 104-105 §439-446 'Accentuation', stated for Manding as a whole (siglum MN = 'malinké du nord ou khassonké' is one of the covered dialect groups): denies lexical tone (§439); §441 'L'accent tonique, caractérisé en mandingue par la hauteur plus que par l'intensité, et très peu marqué en général, tombe comme en français sur la dernière syllabe du mot'; §446 accent not marked because 'soumis à une régularité absolue'. Pan-Manding, pre-tonological, not Khassonké-specific.

sources.note: Family-level only; the volume has no Xasonka chapter (Maninka-Xasonka treated as one language in the overview, p. 17-18). p. 34: 'Ударение в большинстве М.я. отсутствует. Там, где оно может быть выделено (в частности, бамана), его функциональная нагрузка невелика.' and 'Практически все языки манде тональны.. В большинстве языков западной ветви манде имеется два уровневых тона'.
